family_scope_guard: A narrow failure is never treated as rejection of a broader candidate family, untested adaptation, verifier class, benchmark class, or self-improvement method.

assessments.mechanism: Intrinsic prompted self-correction without reliable external correctness feedback can degrade reasoning.
assessments.clean_scope: Matched GSM8K/CommonSenseQA/HotpotQA tests on specified GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Llama-2-era models; not evidence against correction with external verifiers or newer specialized systems.
assessments.uncertainty: Model-generation and task transfer are unresolved.
assessments.o_comparison: O's repair loop uses task evidence/fresh Root cycles rather than assuming intrinsic self-correction, but no matched intrinsic-self-correction experiment was found.

assessments.mechanism: Homogeneous multi-agent debate can lose to equal-response self-consistency at matched response budget.
assessments.clean_scope: Specific gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 GSM8K setup with three agents/two rounds; does not reject heterogeneous/specialized MAS.
assessments.o_comparison: No O multi-agent debate implementation/evaluation matching this setup was found.

assessments.mechanism: Search-time access to benchmark answers/metadata can inflate search-agent benchmark scores.
assessments.clean_scope: Public benchmark/search contamination; leakage rates are environment-specific and do not transfer to private/dynamic tests.
assessments.uncertainty: O has not measured web search-time answer leakage for the cited retrievers/benchmarks.
assessments.o_comparison: O uses redacted/held-out tasks, scorer separation, provenance and contamination-aware fresh executors; exact cited leakage mechanism is not directly measured.

assessments.mechanism: Reusable agent skills can cause functional/efficiency regressions; attribute them with paired no-skill/cheaper controls.
assessments.uncertainty: No reproduction of the cited skill-regression taxonomy exists in O.
assessments.o_comparison: O Candidates are scoped/reversible, preserve protected baselines and cost/risk evidence, but O has not run the paired skill/no-skill benchmark.

assessments.mechanism: Full execution traces can materially improve failure attribution relative to partial observations in multi-agent systems.
assessments.clean_scope: TraceElephant multi-agent attribution; attribution evidence, not direct task-success evidence.
assessments.uncertainty: O has not compared full-versus-partial traces in a matched attribution benchmark.
assessments.o_comparison: O persists invocation/tool events, provenance and outcomes, so the trace-availability submechanism exists, but the cited attribution effect is untested.

assessments.mechanism: Benchmark defects can masquerade as agent failures; benchmark auditing should be a first-class validity check.
assessments.clean_scope: BenchGuard on ScienceAgentBench and BIXBench Verified-50 only.
assessments.uncertainty: No inference to other benchmarks without task-level audit.
assessments.o_comparison: O explicitly treats repository-authored generators/scorers as possible false-positive paths and uses hidden/redacted scoring, but no BenchGuard-like defect auditor/recall measurement exists.

assessments.mechanism: Verifier-guided search can become worse than repeated sampling as compute scales because verifier selection errors compound.
assessments.clean_scope: 2025 math reasoning; Mistral/DeepSeekMath/Qwen2.5-Math 7B, GSM8K/MATH/AIME25, outcome/process verifiers. At sample size 32 reported search-minus-repeated-sampling degradation is ~10pp GSM8K/~20pp MATH for OVM, ~5pp to nearly30pp for PRM; Qwen2.5-Math AIME25 OVM -24.4pp/PRM -22.0pp. >65% of OVM failures in attribution occurred at selection.
assessments.uncertainty: Does not imply all verifier-guided search is inferior; failure is tied to tested verifier/search error and scale.
assessments.o_comparison: O has no verifier-guided beam/tree math search or matched repeated-sampling scaling experiment.

assessments.mechanism: RLVR-trained systems can learn verifier-compatible shortcuts instead of the intended invariant; isomorphic verification can expose/eliminate them.
assessments.clean_scope: ICLR 2026 reasoning-workshop inductive-rule tasks. Reported shortcut counts over 250-case difficulty sets include GPT-5-mini-high 1/24/59 easy/medium/hard and GPT-5-nano 37/147/184; several tested non-RLVR models show zero in the table. Controlled extensional verification induces shortcuts while isomorphic verification removes them.
assessments.uncertainty: Do not generalize shortcut rates or causality to RLVR with fully specified verifiers.
assessments.o_comparison: O has strong evidence-integrity rules but no RLVR training loop or isomorphic verifier test for learned reward shortcuts.

assessments.mechanism: Better static verifier classification can fail to improve RL and can cause downstream regression under policy-distribution shift.
assessments.clean_scope: 2025/ICLR 2026 math case study. Custom verifier recall 0.49→0.62 and precision 0.68→0.73; Skywork-OR1 downstream 58.7→55.5 with the trained verifier; GPQA-Diamond base 36.4, general verifier 45.0, R1-Distill-Verifier 35.9; reward diverges from GPT-4o oracle after ~450 iterations in one run.
assessments.uncertainty: Does not establish model-based verifiers are generally worse than rules; same work contains beneficial hybrids.
assessments.o_comparison: No O RL optimization loop uses a learned verifier as reward, so this dynamic failure has not been tested.

assessments.mechanism: SWE-bench success can be inflated by solution leakage and weak test oracles.
assessments.clean_scope: SWE-Bench+ audit of 251 successful SWE-Agent+GPT-4 patches: 160/251 (63.75%) suspicious; 32.67% answer leak and 31.08% weak-test passes. Removing suspicious fixes drops apparent SWE-bench resolution 12.47%→3.97%, Lite 18.0%→9.33%, Verified 22.4%→10.0%.
assessments.uncertainty: Percentages are for the audited agent/model/benchmark versions, not universal coding-agent failure rates; issue age is contamination risk, not direct proof of training exposure.
assessments.o_comparison: O already uses protected/hidden evidence, scorer separation and contamination-aware boundaries, but has not reproduced this SWE-bench audit.

assessments.mechanism: SWE-bench Verified can measure benchmark memory/exposure as well as localization ability.
assessments.clean_scope: 2025 probe on two Claude models: roughly 3x better localization on SWE-bench Verified than BeetleBox/SWE-rebench and ~6x better edited-file identification without extra project context.
assessments.uncertainty: Commercial training data is unavailable; this is circumstantial, and dataset difficulty may contribute.
assessments.o_comparison: O has contamination-aware held-out/freshness machinery but no cross-benchmark memory-localization probe.

assessments.mechanism: Outcome verifiers can be an attack surface and should be adversarially hardened before treating their scores as capability/reward evidence.
assessments.clean_scope: 2026 terminal-agent benchmark audit: 323/1,968 tasks (16%) hackable. KernelBench held-out exploit attack 62%→0 after hacker-fixer hardening; stronger attackers 76%/61%→0 in that tested setting; Terminal Bench Gemini 3.1 Pro remains 17% after hardening from 39%.
assessments.uncertainty: 16% is suite/access-condition specific; patched verifiers may retain adaptive vulnerability.
assessments.o_comparison: O explicitly refuses to treat repository-authored/internal checks as AGI proof and requires harder independent evidence, so the failure class is known. No hacker-fixer verifier-hardening loop or matched exploit-set experiment exists.

assessments.mechanism: Verifier quality is target-distribution specific; a verifier that improves self-training on one task can regress a new task while training loss improves.
assessments.clean_scope: 2026 VLM self-DPO preprint. Verifiers that help MathVista fall to 8%-23% target-task rubric accuracy on MMMU; every tested sub-threshold verifier regresses the student by 3.4-10.9pp; regression replicated on Qwen-2.5-VL-3B.
assessments.uncertainty: Recent single-author preprint; text-only/general self-improvement replication is pending.
assessments.o_comparison: O already requires exact-scope evidence, protected regressions and no transfer beyond tested conditions, so this non-transfer principle is known; the VLM/verifier ladder itself is untested.

assessments.mechanism: Realistic network/server faults can collapse web-agent success under otherwise matched benchmark runs; generic recovery prompting is not uniformly sufficient.
assessments.clean_scope: WAREX/TMLR 2026. WebArena no-fault 0.124→0.037 network (-70% relative)/0.053 server (-57%); REAL 0.170→0.045 (-73%)/0.071 (-58%); WebVoyager 0.420→0.020 (-95%)/0.300 (-28%). Recovery prompts only partially restore several cells.
assessments.uncertainty: Fault models, agents and benchmark scaffolds are specific; no universal production drop follows.
assessments.o_comparison: O has provider/block recovery policy, but no controlled web-agent network/server fault robustness benchmark or comparable success measurement.

assessments.mechanism: Official benchmark scaffolds can leak test examples and invalidate evaluations; aggregate scores are insufficient without execution/log integrity inspection.
assessments.clean_scope: HAL/ICLR 2026 found the official TAU-bench Few Shot scaffold loaded actual test examples; authors state all evaluations using it were invalidated after about $1,000 spend.
assessments.uncertainty: This invalidates the affected scaffold/file, not all TAU-bench evaluations.
assessments.o_comparison: O already treats contamination/scorer separation/provenance as first-class and does not trust repository-authored test success alone; exact TAU scaffold audit was not run.

assessments.mechanism: Agent benchmark failures can be confounded by scaffold/environment barriers and instruction-interface conflicts; capability attribution should separate these from policy errors.
assessments.clean_scope: HAL analyzed 1,634 transcripts from 36 model-scaffold pairs on AssistantBench/SciCode/CORE-Bench; roughly 40% of failed tasks contained at least one environmental barrier. This is observational, not a causal 40% failure attribution.
assessments.uncertainty: Benchmark-specific and co-occurrence is not causal contribution.
assessments.o_comparison: O separately records provider/evaluator/coordination blocks and fail-closed source errors, but has no matched HAL-style benchmark failure attribution study.

assessments.mechanism: Increasing reasoning effort is non-monotonic for agents under matched model/scaffold/benchmark comparisons.
assessments.clean_scope: HAL/ICLR 2026: 21 of 36 higher-vs-lower/no-reasoning model-agent-benchmark cells had equal or lower accuracy; 15 improved.
assessments.uncertainty: Does not mean reasoning generally hurts; scaffold/task/model interactions and cost differences matter.
assessments.o_comparison: O has one narrow compute-scaling comparison for checkpoint width (1.0→3.0 invocations for only 0.827209s median wall improvement) and explicitly treats added compute as an intervention, but has not tested reasoning-effort scaling itself. This is related partial evidence only, not the HAL result.
